Where your data is, cryptography, recovery
Every request, never keys, passwords or file names
No ads, no tracking: funded by voluntary donations
Cloakroll %1$s. Not affiliated with Amazon or Microsoft; Amazon Photos and OneDrive are trademarks of their owners.

• No ads. No trackers, no analytics, no crash reporting.
• No servers and no accounts of ours: the app talks only to %1$s, only with encrypted files.
• Nothing is collected, so nothing can be sold or leaked by us.
• Free and open source (GPL-3.0): anyone can check what the app does.
• Funded only by voluntary donations. Donating unlocks nothing: every feature is free for everyone.
• %1$s: %2$s, %3$s (big files are several). They also show up in the %1$s app as images of static: that\'s them, don\'t delete them there.

• Folders and list: the folder names, which item is in which, and the list of your items (name, date, size) are saved there as one more encrypted PNG (subfolder \"index\"), so a new phone gets them back with Sync without downloading every file. %1$s can\'t read any of it.
• This phone: the list of items and small previews, both encrypted with your vault key, in app-private storage, excluded from backups and phone-to-phone transfers.
• Sign-in: a Microsoft token, stored encrypted with a key in this phone\'s secure hardware.
• Sign-in: the Amazon session cookies of the sign-in page, in app-private storage.
• Your key: only in memory while unlocked. The app locks itself 60 s after you leave it. A running background upload keeps its own copy of the key until it finishes.

• Your key: only in memory while unlocked; also stored wrapped by a fingerprint-protected key in the phone\'s secure hardware (Android Keystore). The app locks itself 60 s after you leave it. A running background upload keeps its own copy of the key until it finishes.

• Key = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(password, random 16-byte salt, 600 000 iterations).
• Each file: AES-256-GCM with a fresh random nonce. The GCM tag rejects any modified bit.
• Name, date and EXIF are inside the encrypted part.
• Only standard algorithms from Android's built-in crypto library, and no third-party libraries at all.
• Vault salt: %1$s

Download the PNGs of the vault folder from the %1$s website, then on a PC:\npython photovault.py dec <folder> -o out\n(photovault.py is part of Cloakroll\'s open-source code on GitHub.) If you lose the phone: install the app, sign in to the same account, enter the same password; the app restores your vault.
• Files over 32 MB are stored as several encrypted parts; a big video is downloaded completely before it plays.\n• Background jobs are limited by Android to 6 hours per day.

• Amazon has no public API: Cloakroll uses the same web interface as the Amazon Photos website. If Amazon changes it, uploads can stop until the app is updated; stored files stay decryptable, also with photovault.py.
• The vault counts against your OneDrive storage: each PNG is about as big as the original file.

Before you start: what it costs
The key comes from the password, so every file has to be encrypted again with the new key:

• It runs in the background with a notification. Android allows background transfers up to 6 hours a day, so a big vault may need more than one day: it resumes by itself every time you unlock Cloakroll.
• Until it has finished, the files not re-encrypted yet still open with the OLD password. At the end the old password opens nothing in your vault, except copies someone may already have downloaded.
• The old copies go to the %1$s. %2$s
• New uploads wait until the re-encryption has finished (or tap Stop in its notification).
• Fingerprint unlock is switched off; you can switch it on again right after.
• Don't set up Cloakroll on another phone until it has finished.
Photos don\'t use your storage; videos do, and may keep counting until Amazon empties the trash.
They keep counting against your OneDrive storage until the recycle bin is emptied, so OneDrive needs about as much free space as the vault uses.

Tap Add and pick from your gallery. Each file is encrypted on your phone and uploaded as an image of random pixels: the cloud only ever sees noise. The queue runs in the background, with a Stop button.
The gallery shows small previews kept only on your phone. Tap one to download and open the original, swipe for the next, pinch to zoom, Save to phone to export a copy.
Long-press to select items, then move them to a folder or delete them. Folders and the item list are saved to your storage too, encrypted, so another phone gets them back.
The vault locks itself 60 s after you leave the app, and nothing decrypted stays on screen. Fingerprint unlock is optional, in Settings.
In Settings, Automatic backup sends new photos and videos by itself on Wi-Fi, even with the app closed. Free up space removes from the phone what the vault already holds.
On a new phone, sign in to the same storage, enter the same password and Sync brings everything back in seconds. Nobody can recover the photos without the password, not even us: keep it safe.

What the app does with your data: nothing leaves your phone unencrypted, nothing reaches us

Cloakroll is free, with no ads and no tracking, and it is kept going only by voluntary donations. If it is useful to you, a small donation helps keep it maintained. Donating unlocks nothing: everything stays free for everyone.

On GitHub you also find the source code and photovault.py, a small Python program that opens your vault on a PC, without the app.
